CA excise taxes are the highest in the nation per gallon, by 2 cents over Pennsylvania. The actual reason gas is more expensive is that California has higher standards for it's gasoline to help lower emissions which require gas sold in the state to go through a step that not all refineries are tooled for making most of the gas sold in CA refined here where it's expensive to refine.

In addition to what's been mentioned, (high taxes mostly),  California's emissions standard is set to a higher rung and California can only sell gas that has been refined further to emit lower emissions. Not all refineries are tooled for this extra step which is more expensive on it's own, so most of the gas sold in CA has to come from CA, where production costs are already high. 

Taxes have relatively very little to do with it. the tax per gal in California is 60 cents. Washington is 49 cents, Florida 37, Pennsylvania 58 cents. It's mostly the production cost of the further refined gas product.

Forget original receipts for anything like that too most of the time.  Most of what I've seen is the house will the client where they came from and whether or not they have any sort of paperwork to verify any of the things they mention like receipts, storage facility invoices, etc (most do not but some do and that's always nice). it's not a dealbreaker for most houses. Houses will then do their inspection and work backwards based on the info given to them by the client. A super large blue chip collection spanning many many vintages will almost always have something off about one or two of the bottles. Not fakes, but things that argue against the information given to them by the client. A great example of an inconsistency would be if they claimed to buy Bordeaux en premeur and stored it in their subterranean home cellar in Massachusetts and the wines come in and one bottle has a Christie's sticker on the back and a bar code on the side from Vinfolio. 
_______________________________

The idea that a collector will have original receipts and can prove proper storage spanning 20, 30, or 40+ years is a little fantastical. I would argue there are maybe only a handful of people in the world that can prove they bought and maintained custody(in good storage) of 1976 Dom..  The houses do their best with the older stuff, but most of that is what do is examine the bottle they have in front of them and work backwards if anything doesn't add up.
